newsitem.title: NEPAL: Scottish climber's body flown to Kathmandu.
newsitem.headline: Scottish climber's body flown to Kathmandu.

text.p: The body of a Scottish climber who died on Mount Everest was flown on Thursday to the Nepali capital by an army helicopter, a trekking agency official said.

Malcolm Duff, a 43-year-old professional climber from Culross, Fife, was found dead in his tent in an overnight camp at the base of the world's highest mountain by a Sherpa guide who went to give him morning tea on Wednesday.

"The body will be kept at the German embassy freezer until family members arrive," said Chhwang Sherpa, managing director of Arun Treks and Expeditions, which was handling the seven-member team that Duff was leading.
Sherpa said the climber's family wanted to take the body to Britain.

A doctor's report from the base camp to Nepal's Tourism Ministry, which oversees climbing activities in the Himalayan kingdom, said vomit was found in Duff's mouth and air passage, and he had suffered a "secondary cardio-respiratory attack."
Duff is the first climber to die on the way to Everest since the current spring climbing season began in March.
As many as 12 teams are trying to climb the 8,848-metre (29,028-foot) peak this season.
Eight people were killed in the climbing season last year when blizzards hit the region. Five died on the Nepali side and the other three on the Tibetan side to the north of the peak.
Major Kisendra Bahadur Shahi, the pilot of the army helicopter that picked up Duff's body from the 5,350 metre-high (17,500-ft) base camp, said about 200 climbers and guides were at the camp.
"The weather is beautiful and I could see climbers going from base camp to Camp One," Shahi told Reuters after flying Duff's body to Kathmandu.
Duff is the 10th Briton to be killed on Everest, where 148 people of various nationalities have lost their lives since the early 1920s when attempts to scale the peak were first recorded.
